speaker: Ghulam Nabi Azad
role: Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare
quote_original: Maternal mortality rate has declined from 301 per 100,000 live births in 2001-03 to 254 in 2004-05 and further declined to 212 in 2007-09.
quote_english: Maternal mortality rate has declined from 301 per 100,000 live births in 2001-03 to 254 in 2004-05 and further declined to 212 in 2007-09.
summary: The SRS special bulletin for 2007-09 estimated India's maternal mortality ratio at 212 per 100,000 live births, down from 254 in 2004-06; the 2001-03 estimate was 301.

govt_response.title: PIB: SRS maternal mortality estimates 2007-09
govt_response.summary: The government release confirms the decline from 254 to 212 and attributes it to the SRS special bulletin.

analysis:
The statement cites SRS estimates: MMR 301 in 2001-03, 254 in 2004-06 and 212 in 2007-09. The SRS special bulletin for 2007-09, published in June 2011, reports an MMR of 212 with a 95 per cent confidence interval of 198-226.

The same bulletin reports the decline from 254 to 212, a fall of about 17 per cent. The 301 figure for 2001-03 is consistent with the earlier SRS series.

The claim is a statistical statement about published SRS estimates and is supported by the primary bulletin.
